stories.title: Forest loss, wildfires in Indonesia put orangutans at high extinction risk
summary: Orangutan populations are at a higher risk of extinction amid soaring forest loss and raging wildfires across key habitats in Sumatra and Kalimantan, as the world struggles to keep up with the global target of halting biodiversity loss by 2030.

In a joint report published on Oct 24, environmental groups Mighty Earth and Satya Bumi issued a “red code” warning for the Tapanuli orangutan, often considered world’s rarest great ape, which is facing a higher extinction risk.
Both the mine and the power plant intersect with the geographical range of the Tapanuli orangutan in Batang Toru.

stories.title: Bangladesh presses India before Ganges water treaty expires
summary: With a 30-year Ganges water-sharing treaty with India expiring in December, Bangladesh fears failure to strike a new deal could deepen water shortages, threatening tens of millions of livelihoods.
Water arguments over 54 cross-border rivers between India and Bangladesh stretch back decades, and the Ganges is among the most important.
Bangladesh accused India of diverting most of the water.

stories.title: At least 5 killed, over two dozen injured as bus plunges into drain in Punjab's Hafizabad
summary: LAHORE: At least five people were killed and 27 others injured when a passenger bus plunged into a drain in Punjab’s Hafizabad district on Thursday, according to Rescue 1122.
Five rescue vehicles participated in the operation, Rescue 1122 said.

The accident occurred two days after 10 people were killed and 44 others injured when a passenger bus overturned after hitting a road divider in Rajanpur district’s Rojhan tehsil on the Indus Highway on Wednesday.

stories.title: Punjab govt has 1m tonnes of wheat for five months, provincial assembly told
summary: LAHORE: The Punjab Assembly was told on Wednesday that the provincial government had over one million tonnes of wheat in stock for the next five months as opposition members raised concerns over rising flour prices, delayed development funds and the plight of farmers.
More than 1.5m bags of wheat arrived in Punjab markets daily, while the government had over 1m tonnes of grain in stock to meet requirements for the next five months, she told the house.

Replying to a question by treasury member Amjad Ali Javed, the food minister said the government had cancelled the licences of 90 out of 185 private markets following complaints of fraud against citizens in the name of such markets.

stories.title: Fake MoFA official arrested in Gujrat
summary: GUJRAT: The Federal Investigation Agency (FIA) claimed on Wednesday to have arrested a fake official of the Foreign Affairs Liaison Office (FALO), Gujrat, when he was allegedly demanding bribes from the applicants for the attestation of their documents.
An FIA official said that the role of other agents, Gujrat officials of MoFA and other departments would also be probed during the investigation.

Earlier, in March this year, the MoFA had removed the head of Gujrat FALO and two other officials on the complaints of corruption in the attestation of documents after a junior official lodged a case of Rs4 million theft at his flat located near the office.

stories.title: Punjab CM announces establishment of Apna Kisan Bank
summary: LAHORE: Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz on Wednesday announced the establishment of the province’s first ‘Apna Kisan Bank’ and agricultural loans worth Rs17 billion and an increase in financing under the Kisan Card scheme.
Farmers can get loans up to Rs50m at 5pc markup; Kisan Card limit increased The CM said the Rs17bn in subsidised loans would benefit farmers cultivating around five million acres.
She said the government had resisted pressure to impose agricultural income tax on farmers and was committed to protecting their interests.

stories.title: Turkish Maarif Foundation: Lahore High Court sets aside labour court order
summary: LAHORE: The Lahore High Court (LHC) has set aside orders of a labour court and a wages authority against the Turkish Maarif Foundation in a claim filed by a former vice-principal.
The Wages Authority awarded her Rs10.8 million, and the labour court dismissed the foundation’s appeal for non-appearance and non-deposit of the decreed amount.

Justice Hassan directed the authority to decide the matter afresh, especially the preliminary issues, in light of the case’s background, Pakistan-Turkiye relations and the foundation’s legal status as recognised in the Supreme Court’s judgement of December 2018.

stories.title: 294 Sahiwal farmers booked for water theft in five months
summary: At Chak 63/5-L, a farmer, Sadiq, allegedly broke a water outlet (moga) and diverted irrigation water to his fields and those of other shareholders.

stories.title: Child’s kidnapping, murder suspects killed in ‘encounter’ in Muridke
summary: TOBA TEK SINGH: Police claimed that two suspects in a kidnapping for ransom and murder of a five-year-old boy were killed in an encounter late on Tuesday night.
Police claimed the attackers attempted to free the suspects and during the exchange of fire, both the detained suspects sustained injuries and died on the spot.

Police claimed that on Tuesday night, the body of the missing child was recovered from the village’s pond on the suspects’ lead, who had allegedly weighed down the sack by putting bricks in it so that the body could not float.

stories.title: Court rejects plea to add murder, terrorism charges in Karachi's Gul Plaza fire case
summary: KARACHI: Rejecting an application seeking the addition of murder and terrorism charges, a judicial magistrate accepted the charge sheet in the Gul Plaza fire case on Wednesday, in which the police blamed the building management’s “negligence”.
Judicial Magistrate (South) Aasim Aslam pronounced his order on Wednesday, in which he accepted the final charge sheet filed by the second investigating officer of the case.

The IO chargesheeted four members of Gul Plaza Management Committee — Tanveer Pasta, Amar Ismail, Muhammad Ramazan and Muhammad Ameen — and the owner of an artificial flower shop, Naimatullah, and his over 11-year-old son Huzaifa in the case.

stories.title: Islamabad's Capital Development Authority to start Shahdara Dam project soon
summary: ISLAMABAD: The Capital Development Authority (CDA) on Wednesday announced that construction of the Shahdara Dam project would begin soon.

The water demand of Islamabad is around 250 million gallons per day (MGD), while the CDA supplies approximately 70 MGD, mostly to the urban population, through three main sources, including Khanpur Dam, Simly Dam and tubewells.

Meanwhile, every year during the monsoon, the CDA releases large quantities of water from Simly Dam, while Rawalpindi authorities also release water from Rawal Dam, which is located in Islamabad but supplies water to the city’s residents.

stories.title: Moscow’s Afghan outreach
summary: The question is not whether Moscow will replace Islamabad as Kabul’s principal interlocutor, but whether Russia’s expanding diplomatic, security and economic engagement will give the Taliban greater room to manoeuvre in their dealings with Pakistan.
Its expanding relations with Moscow also offer the Taliban another channel for diplomatic engagement, security cooperation, and economic opportunity.
Although the Taliban also oppose IS-K, this convergence does not necessarily mean Moscow will place Pakistan’s concerns about the TTP at the centre of its Afghan policy.

stories.title: A huddle in Tehran
summary: LAST month, I argued in this space that Iran is emerging as a big regional power to our west.
On Oct 26, Saudi Arabia’s defence minister, Pakistan’s defence chief, and Turkiye’s intellige­nce chief sat down in Tehran with Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council.
In May, Saudi Arabia itself floated a non-aggression pact between Iran and the states of the region, reportedly modelled on the 1975 Helsinki Accords.

stories.title: Commodity prices to surge 23pc, warns World Bank
summary: Oil, natural gas, food and metals prices all rose sharply this year as global shocks mounted, the World Bank said in its latest Commodity Markets Outlook.

Commodity prices were expected to ease by 7pc next year, it said, but continued shocks — including forecasts for the worst El Nino weather effect since 1950 — could keep food commodity prices elevated, raising the spectre of higher inflation and tighter monetary policy.

An adverse scenario that coupled a record El Nino, more Black Sea grain shipment disruptions, escalation in the Middle East conflict and ongoing damage to Russian oil infrastructure could drive food prices 12pc higher than expected, it said.

summary: ISLAMABAD: Religi­ous scholars, spiritual lea­ders and representatives of different faiths have unanimously reaffirmed their support for a decree against terrorism, suicide attacks, and extremism while fully endorsing the national narrative of Paigham-i-Pakistan.
The declaration was iss­ued at a joint meeting org­anised by the National Paigham-i-Amn Commit­tee and the Balochistan Provincial Paigham-i-Amn Committee at Jamia Sala­fia Dawat-ul-Haq.

The declaration expres­sed support for the national security institutions in their fight against Fitna al-Khawarij and Fitna al-Hindustan, saying safeguarding national security and eliminating terrorism were shared responsibilities.

stories.title: Arrest warrants for Sohail Afridi, others out in Radio Pakistan attack case
summary: PESHAWAR: An anti-terrorism court on Wednesday issued arrest warrants for Sohail Afridi, the ex-chief minister who was rendered nonfunctional after the imposition of governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, and four other PTI leaders in the Radio Pakistan attack case.

The court order stated that the police had submitted a supplementary charge-sheet against the five accused, who had not been arrested, and directed that warrants be issued under Section 204 of the Code of Criminal Procedure.

According to investigation officer DSP Khushal Khan’s report, Radio Pakistan Peshawar station director Tufail Ahmad recorded a supplementary statement in light of the forensic findings, nominating the five men as accused.

stories.title: Safety net foils drone attack on Hassankhel police station
summary: PESHAWAR: An anti-drone net saved Hassankhel police station after a quadcopter dropped an improvised explosive device (IED) on the building.
The bomb, however, did not reach the roof due to the anti-drone net installed over the facility’s rooftop. “It was a locally manufactured IED and was dropped from a quadcopter.
The anti-drone net installed over the rooftop protected the building,” SP Saddar division Fida Hussain told Dawn.

stories.title: Dir traders stage protest as anti-encroachment drive continues
summary: LOWER DIR/LAKKI MARWAT: Traders and political activists staged a demonstration in Rabat Bazaar on Wednesday, asking the authorities to resolve the dispute over the road’s width, as the Lower Dir administration continued its anti-encroachment drive across the district.
It noted that the NHA had previously communicated a road width of 40 feet to the assistant settlement officer through a letter dated July 9, 2024, which now required correction.

Deputy commissioner Shahid Rafiq said the administration cleared roads from temporary and permanent encroachments in the town. “The successful anti-encroachment operation will help ease traffic on the Indus Highway,” he added.

stories.title: 45 Nust researchers ranked among top 2pc of global scientists
summary: ISLAMABAD: As many as 45 researchers from the National University of Sciences and Technology (Nust) have earned the prestigious honour of being among the world’s top 2pc of scientists in 2026, say rankings compiled by Stanford University and Elsevier.

According to a press release issued by Nust, the distinction places Nust researchers among an international community of leading scholars whose work is contributing immensely to the advancement of knowledge and scientific progress across diverse disciplines.

stories.title: Seven killed, five injured as ambulance catches fire at Thar hospital
summary: MITHI: Seven people were burnt to death while five others suffered severe burns when an oxygen cylinder exploded in an ambulance at a Peoples Primary Healthcare Initiative (PPHI)-run hospital in Dano Dhandhal in Tharparkar’s Nagarparkar taluka, rescue officials and police said.
According to rescue personnel, hospital staff were preparing patients for transfer and connecting an oxygen cylinder inside the ambulance when it exploded, setting the vehicle ablaze.
Police attributed the incident to an oxygen cylinder explosion and said patients and hospital employees were among the dead and injured.

stories.title: Antonelli on brink of F1 title
summary: Kimi Antonelli will take his place in Formula One’s record books as the youngest champion and Italy’s first since 1953, barring a wild swing of unexpected misfortunes amid a fiesta atmosphere at this weekend’s Mexico City Grand Prix.

Almost more remarkably, he will also succeed Italy's last champion Alberto Ascari, who won for Ferrari in 1953, after a gap of 73 years during which his country has become synonymous with Formula One.
He has triumphed five times in Mexico and won twice before last Sunday’s race in Austin while world champion Lando Norris won from pole last year for McLaren and is due a change in fortunes.
